title: Intermittent No Start
summary: Practical workflow for no-start complaints that come and go, separating battery, starter circuit, fuel, and immobilizer clues.
intro: Intermittent no-start diagnosis depends on whether the engine does not crank, cranks but will not start, or starts after sitting. Capturing voltage, command, and fuel/spark state during the failure matters most.
common_sounds: No crank, single click, or rapid clicking
Cranks normally but does not fire
Starts later after sitting or cooling down
Security light, low battery, or fuel pump prime may be inconsistent
quick_checks: Load test battery and voltage-drop cables during failure
Check starter command, relay, fuse, and ground path
Verify spark, injector pulse, and fuel pressure during crank-no-start
Note security light or key recognition issues
inspection_priority: Capture the failure state before replacing parts
Battery and cable checks first for no-crank
Fuel pressure and spark checks first for crank-no-start
confidence_cues: No-crank and crank-no-start are different paths
common_causes: Starter solenoid, relay, or command circuit fault
Crank sensor, immobilizer, or wiring issue

diagnostic_path_sections.title: No-Crank Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when the engine does not turn over during the failure.
checks: Load test battery and check terminal fit
Check relay, fuse, neutral safety, and crank command

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Crank-No-Start Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when crank speed is normal but the engine does not fire.
checks: Scan for crank/cam, immobilizer, and fuel control codes
